segments.text: Section 3. You're going to listen to a conversation between a professor and a student, but first
you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24. Now listen carefully and answer questions
21 to 24. Come on in. Oh, hi Linda, come have a seat.
Good afternoon Mr Xavier. I received your email telling me to come in to talk about
my team presentation this morning. Is something wrong?
No, no, nothing's wrong. I just want to ask for your opinion about your team members contribution
to the teamwork so that I can mark them properly. Now, as the team leader, what do you have
to say about your team mates? Give me some information on both the pros and the cons of
each person.
Oh, yes, of course. Well, let me see. I will go with me first. Having been familiar with
the leadership position I'm pretty confident with the way I assigned the
tasks for my team. However, dealing with people now is much more challenging than
it used to be since this group have stronger opinions than the last. I think
I need to work more on that if I want to keep my leadership role. Right, well
being a leader has never been an easy job and what about the others anyway?
Well, do you remember know-it-all Karen? The one who always raises her hand when
you ask a question. Oh yeah, I remember. The girl with curly blonde hair. Oh isn't
she such a great asset to your team? She is indeed. She's in charge of most of
the content of the presentation. She did a great job writing a concise summary
of the chapter. However, what she lacks is a sense of teamwork. She worked
without taking other members' opinions into account and criticized everyone's work. She
seemed to regard us as her inferiors. I had a difficult time dealing with her.
You'll find yourself in that situation if you want to be in management, to be honest.
There are lots of people like that out there. You have to balance their effectiveness and
their ego at the same time, which is never easy.
Yeah, different people have different characteristics.
Take Lee as an example, he's too quiet
and I could barely make him speak during team meetings.
He gave almost no opinion at all.
I had to spend lots of time breaking the ice
between him and the rest of the team.
Gradually, he opened up to everyone
and I found out that he's really good with computer skills.
All the effects in our slideshow were made by him
they are amazing. Well good job getting him involved Linda. Thanks and then
there's Louis. He's the least disciplined member of our team. He was often late for
team meetings and he had thousands of reasons for that. Despite his persistent
lateness he has a smooth French accent which is very charming. It was effective
in drawing the whole class's attention and I have to admit it did improve the
presentation a lot. Well I guess you can say he's the speaker of your team and
everyone loves a French accent don't they? As far as I can see your team did a
very good job overall. Thank you professor. Before you listen to the rest
of the message you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30. Now listen
carefully and answer questions 25 to 30. Also now that you're here I have a few
questions to ask do you mind? Not at all professor. I was wondering what are the
three qualities that you consider most important in a good leader? I've never
really put a serious thought to this just give me a moment. Yeah yeah yeah
take your time don't worry the question just came out of curiosity. Right even
though I'm confident with my ability to delegate I think effective communication
is the most important quality. A good leader needs to be able to communicate
in a variety of ways from transmitting information to coaching people and they
must be able to listen to and communicate with a wide range of people
across roles, social identities and more. Hmm yeah interesting choice. What do
you think about integrity? It's often mentioned first when we talk about
leaders traits. I totally agree with the strong morality parts but I think being
honest is overrated. You need to be flexible sometimes you know telling
white lies for a greater good a bigger picture. I see. Considering my leadership
style I'd say a good leader also needs to have influence on followers as well
respect for them. I love to bond with my teammates and these characteristics suit
me well. Thank you so much for your honest answer Linda. Now I'd like to give
you some advice on what traits you need to improve. Is that alright with you? Of
course, yes please. I never pass on an opportunity to improve myself. Ah good
good, that's the quality of self-awareness right now and apparently
that's not what you need to improve on. What I have in mind is actually
learning agility. It's the ability to know what to do when you don't know what
to do. And it will help me excel in unfamiliar circumstances which leaders
face a lot. Yes and another necessary quality for you is courage. It enables
leaders to step up and move things in the right direction rather than avoiding
problems or allowing conflicts to fester. It means I can give honest
feedback about a bad job or flag a concern for my boss. That's right, yeah and last but not least
you need to show more innovation. It's not that you have to be a creative genius with thought
provoking ideas but rather you need to give others the freedom to develop their own ideas.
Your job is to be open to new ideas and also discussions. Thank you very much for your
wisdom. Now I know what I need to work on to become a good leader.
You're welcome. Anyway, now I have to attend a meeting.
If you have any more questions, email me and I'll get back to you as soon as I
can. I will. Goodbye. That's the end of
section three. You now have 30 seconds to check your
answers to section three. Now turn to section four.
